We need to generate unit test code for findRecord method covering all cases from JSON. The provided test class already has some tests but we need to add more to cover all groups, using reflection for the case where internal sections array is null. Also need to handle null record case, duplicate records, etc.

We must not modify @Before/@After. We'll add new test methods, possibly parameterized.

We need imports for reflection, InetAddress, etc. Also need to create ARecord objects; there is class ARecord extends Record. Use ARecord constructor: ARecord(Name name, int dclass, long ttl, InetAddress address). Use DClass.IN.

We need to ensure we can add records to sections using addRecord.

For null list scenario: we need to simulate sections[section] == null. The Message constructor probably initializes sections array with null entries; addRecord may allocate list. To make null list, we can ensure we never added any record to that section, but the code checks (sections[section] != null) && sections[section].contains(r). If sections[section] is null, returns false. That's already covered by empty section test. However there is group "Valid section – empty list (null) → record not found" which is same.

But there is also "Uninitialized sections array → NullPointerException" where sections field itself is null. Need to set via reflection: set the private field "sections" to null. Then call findRecord; expecting NPE.

Also test for null record argument: findRecord(null, section) should return false (no exception). Implementation: sections[section].contains(null) returns false if list present. If sections[section] null, also false.

We'll write tests:

- testFindRecord_NullRecord_ReturnsFalse (section non-null list). Use addRecord aRecord to section, then call findRecord(null, Section.QUESTION) expecting false.

- testFindRecord_NullRecordAndNullList_ReturnsFalse: need both record null and internal list null. Ensure we haven't added any record; sections[section] is null. Call findRecord(null, Section.QUESTION). Expect false.

- testFindRecord_ValidSectionEmptyList_ReturnsFalse: Already covered but we can keep.

- testFindRecord_ListContainsDuplicate_ReturnsTrue: add same record twice to section, then findRecord(record, section) true.

- testFindRecord_RecordPresentDifferentInstance_ReturnsTrue: create new ARecord with same fields as aRecord added earlier; should be equal.

- testFindRecord_SameNameTypeDifferentData_ReturnsFalse: add aRecord with address 1.2.3.4 to section, then create new ARecord with same name, type, ttl but different address 9.9.9.9, findRecord should be false.

- testFindRecord_RecordPresentInDifferentSection_ReturnsFalse: add to ANSWER, query AUTHORITY.

- testFindRecord_InvalidSection_Negative_Throws: already have invalid positive test; add negative.

- testFindRecord_InvalidSection_OutOfRange_Throws: already have.

- testFindRecord_UninitializedSectionsArray_ThrowsNPE: use reflection.

- testFindRecord_ValidSection_EmptyArrayListSizeZero_ReturnsFalse: ensure list is initialized but empty. To get empty list, we can call message.getSection(Section.ANSWER) maybe returns empty list? addRecord not called. But sections[section] may be null. To force empty list but not null, we can use reflection to set sections[section] = new ArrayList<>(); but we should avoid private fields. Could use addRecord then removeRecord? Not ideal. Could use reflection to set sections[section] to new ArrayList<>(); This is allowed because we need to test that condition. Use reflection.

But we can also call message.removeAllRecords(section) which may set list to null? Not sure. The test case expects empty list size 0 (non-null). We'll use reflection.

We'll add parameterized tests for groups with similar patterns? Could use @ParameterizedTest with MethodSource.

But simpler: separate test methods.

We need imports: org.junit.jupiter.api.*, org.junit.jupiter.params.*, org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.*, java.net.InetAddress, java.lang.reflect.Field, java.util.ArrayList.

Also need to import org.xbill.DNS.*;.

Now produce final test class code.

We'll keep existing tests unchanged, add new ones.

Make class name Message_findRecord_Test (already). Add new methods.

Make sure to handle exceptions: reflection may throw NoSuchFieldException, IllegalAccessException; wrap in try-catch or declare throws Exception.

JUnit5 test methods can declare throws Exception.

Now craft code.
